title: China's Rainbow Mountains Look Fake — But Zhangye Danxia Is Real | China Travel Expert
description:
Every time this place goes viral, half the comments say it's fake or painted. It isn't. This is Zhangye Danxia in Gansu, northwest China — and the stripes are real rock.

Each band is a different mineral staining the sandstone: rust-red from hematite (iron oxide), yellows and browns from limonite and goethite, greens from chlorite, all carried in by groundwater over an immense span of time. The sediments were laid down over tens of millions of years, then tilted up as the Indian plate crashed into Asia and carved into ridges by wind and water.

Honest catch: a lot of the most saturated photos you've seen ARE boosted in editing — but the layered colour is genuinely there in the rock. Zhangye Danxia was designated a UNESCO Global Geopark in 2020.

★ Expert Tip: go late afternoon just before sunset, and after rain if you can. Low side-light and a bit of moisture make the real colours far richer — that's when it looks the way the (honest) photos do, no filter needed.

张掖丹霞（甘肃）常被说成是"假的/修出来的"，其实条纹全是真岩石：赤铁矿染出铁锈红，褐铁矿/针铁矿染黄，绿泥石染绿，地下水带着矿物沉积上色。沉积历时数千万年，印度板块撞上亚洲时被抬升、再被风水侵蚀成这样。很多爆款照片确实调过色，但岩层的颜色是真的。你会去看吗？
